concern_details.detail: main components involved in seat booking and their responsibilities
concern_details.why: Every component on the makeReservation path is there, each with a one-line responsibility: both UIs, LibraryFacade, ReservationManager, AssignmentStrategy, StudyRoomManager, the two model groups, the registries and persistence. The note listing today's rules matches ReservationManager.resolveRoom, resolveTimeSlot, validateUniqueness and selectSeat (ReservationManager.java:65-101, 173-197, 357-400). The view does not show that the booking request enters as ReservationRequestDTO, which is the data a new rule would most likely extend.

concern_details.detail: how they interact with each other
concern_details.why: The main call chain UI -> LibraryFacade -> ReservationManager -> strategy/models/registries is right. Two things are wrong or missing. StudyRoomManager has no edge to the study-room model, but it calls room.isOpenOnDate and computes seat availability per area (StudyRoomManager.java:231, 282-290), so the view hides that availability is computed in two places. NotificationManager -> Registries 'reads reservations' comes from the reminder/expiry job (NotificationManager.java:73-82, getEndingReservations), which is not part of booking. The arrows are also bare 'calls'/'notifies' with no interface, so the developer cannot see which operations (makeReservation(ReservationRequestDTO), selectSeat(List<Seat>)) form the contract.

concern_details.detail: which parts of the system may be affected by the modification
concern_details.why: Highlighting ReservationManager, AssignmentStrategy and the two models is a good start. But the diagram leaves out the shared availability logic a new rule would have to stay consistent with: Seat.isAvailable/Area.getAvailableSeats and ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot (ACTIVE/CONFIRMED) are used both by ReservationManager and by StudyRoomManager, which feeds the wizard's seat counts and seat lists (AreaSelection.java:86, TimeSlotSelection.java:87). StudyRoomManager is therefore also affected, yet it is not marked. The impact on the UIs and REST controller through ReservationRequestDTO appears only as a README inference, not in the view. The existing MakeReservationTest is not mentioned anywhere.

level_why: For a balanced view of one feature, the bottom of the stack has more parts than the concern needs, while the decision-relevant middle has too little. PersistenceManager and the MySQL database add nothing to where rules go or what they affect; they can be merged into the Registries box (as '(JPA/MySQL)') or dropped. The NotificationManager -> Registries edge belongs to the reminder scheduler and should go. The Reservation model -> NotificationManager edge repeats ReservationManager -> NotificationManager (ReservationManager attaches the observer and triggers notifyObservers, ReservationManager.java:120-123), so keep just one. That brings the view to about 10 elements and 11 relations, with room for the one missing edge without going past balanced.
unsupported: NotificationManager -> Registries 'reads reservations' as part of seat booking: the code reads ReservationRegistry only in the end-of-reservation/reminder routine (NotificationManager.java:73-82), not on the makeReservation path.

Reservation model -> NotificationManager 'notifies observers' as a static dependency: Reservation depends only on the Observer interface via Subject (Reservation.java:16, 181); the NotificationManager instance is attached at runtime by ReservationManager (ReservationManager.java:121). The edge should target the Observer interface or be dropped in favour of ReservationManager -> NotificationManager.
missing: StudyRoomManager -> Study-room model dependency (StudyRoomManager.java:231 isOpenOnDate, 282-290 per-seat availability for RoomDetailDTO), and StudyRoomManager marked as affected, because availability shown to students has to follow the same rules as booking.

The booking request contract: LibraryFacade/ReservationManager offering makeReservation(ReservationRequestDTO) (LibraryFacade.java:136, ReservationManager.java:65), required by the Swing wizard (ReservationSummary.java:100) and ReservationController (ReservationController.java:29). A rule that needs new input changes this DTO and both callers.

The shared 'slot occupied' rule in ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot (ReservationRegistry.java:120-123), used by Seat.isAvailable, Student uniqueness and StudyRoomManager: Registries should be marked as affected or the note should name it.
uml: AssignmentStrategy is a Java interface with one implementation, FirstAvailableAssignment (README admits this). Draw it as an interface that ReservationManager requires and FirstAvailableAssignment (or a strategy component) provides, using ball-and-socket or an «interface» element, not as a plain component.

Relations are solid open-arrow lines (PlantUML '-->'), which read as associations. Inter-component usage in a UML component diagram is a dashed dependency (optionally «use»), or an assembly connector between required and provided interfaces.
No provided/required interfaces appear anywhere, even though LibraryFacade exists precisely to be the provided interface. Add at least the booking interface on LibraryFacade/ReservationManager.

The model groups and registries are sets of classes shown as components with no stereotype. That is acceptable, but the merged 'Registries' box should say it is a grouping (for example by naming the three classes as parts), so it does not read as one deployable component.
fixes: Show and mark the shared availability logic: add StudyRoomManager -> Study-room model, mark StudyRoomManager as affected, and name ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot / Seat.isAvailable as rule points in the note.

Model the booking contract as an interface: makeReservation(ReservationRequestDTO) provided by LibraryFacade/ReservationManager and required by the Swing wizard and REST controller, so the impact on callers appears in the view rather than only in the README.
Draw AssignmentStrategy as an interface required by ReservationManager and implemented by FirstAvailableAssignment, and change the solid arrows to dashed dependencies (or assembly connectors).
Remove the off-feature NotificationManager -> Registries edge, and either drop Reservation model -> NotificationManager or retarget it to the Observer interface.
Merge PersistenceManager and the MySQL database into the Registries box (or drop them) to keep the view at the balanced level.
